Process Modelling 
Process modelling creates a visual 
representation of how activities, 
decisions, information, and stakeholders 
interact within a business process.

pages.text:
Process Modelling contains critical insights of a particular process 
including: 
•
Event and activities occur within a workflow
•
Stakeholders involved in the process 
•
Decision points and different paths workflows can take 
•
Timelines of the overall process and each step in the process
What is Process Modelling?

pages.text:
BPMN Basic Notations
Pools
Represents a major participant or organisation 
involved in the process.
→ Example: Customer / Company / Supplier…
Lane
Divides a pool into departments, roles, or systems 
responsible for different activities.
→ Example: Sales / Finance / Warehouse / HR…

Questions for Analysis: 
•
Any steps in the process that frequently cause delays? 
•
Any tasks that are repeated unnecessarily? 
•
Could technology be used to automate or streamline any steps in 
the process?
•
How can the process be improved to enhance the customer 
experience?
•
Who are the key participants?

pages.text:
Working in group, select one of the provided cases below or choose 
your own process. 
1. Identify all key steps, decision points and stakeholders involved 
in the selected process.
2. Create a BPMN diagram using LucidChart or Draw.io
3. Analyse the process and identify potential bottlenecks/ 
inefficiencies areas. 
4. Present your work to class. 
In-class Activity
